To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the probability of underesting string length is a function of the interletter spacing.
the underestimation of letter string lengths in letter crowding is due to the point spread function and the spatial uncertainty of the eye.

the crowding effect is a combination of the following three factors: (1) a reduction of the perceived size of the letters, (2) a reduction of perceived spacing between the letters, and (3) a tendency to underestimate the number of letters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the perceptual mechanisms that are responsible for the letter string shortening effect.
the effect of letter spacing on letter identification.
how the visual system processes the spatial distribution of letters in a string and how the visual system represents a string length.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the underestimation of the length of a string concomitant with the letter crowding effect is a consequence of the point spread of light in the eye.
the crowding effect is not a simple spatial uncertainty effect.
the crowding effect is a combination of the point spread effect and the letter merging effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, when the letters in a string are crowded together, the string is perceived to be shorter, and the letters are perceived to be smaller.
, under conditions of crowding, the letter string is not perceived as a string but is rather perceived as a collection of individual letters.
letter string shortening occurs when letters are close to the limit of visual acuity, when interletter spacings become small, and when the letters are closely packed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the visual system has an inherent bias to underestimate the length and complexity of crowded letter strings.
the crowding effect may be more than a simple letter recognition phenomenon; rather, it may be a more global perceptual process.
the visual system is sensitive to the spatial distribution of letter features, and that the crowding effect can cause letter strings to appear shorter than their true length.
